While bundlers may split these into separate chunks, on the server all chunks get loaded into memory anyway when the module is first imported, and the promises all start resolving concurrently. The stated goal of the PR ("Async import of the appStore packages") is presumably to reduce initial bundle size / startup time, but eagerly calling import() for every app at module scope means every serverless function / server process that imports appStore (directly or transitively — and it's imported by videoClient, getCalendar, payment handlers, etc., which are on hot paths) will load all app modules. True lazy loading would require wrapping each in a thunk: `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and awaiting `appStore[key]()`. As written, this provides no server-side memory/CPU benefit and may increase startup latency due to 29 concurrent module resolutions.
